verdicts.decision_note: The client supplies the initial complete FAQ copy to render on the site, including purchasing, referral, prize, wallet, fee, transfer, and support explanations.
The client explicitly replaces the rendered FAQ with a revised complete version and permits minor editorial refinement before publication.
The supplied product copy changes the no-code reward recipient from a generic NFT holder to an existing ticket holder, requiring the published explanation to remain consistent.
The changed Small and Big Block winner counts and sales triggers make the previously approved FAQ figures obsolete.
The client explicitly requests a new fiat-buyer FAQ section covering Transak wallet creation, authentication, commissions, tickets, notifications, and automatic prize payout.
Removing Big Blocks and changing the purchase allocation necessarily removes obsolete Big Block references and updates the rendered FAQ's reward explanation.
The client explicitly adds and revises FAQ sections explaining fiat-buyer rewards, beginner collection, wallet access, ticket assignment, notifications, payouts, and Chainlink VRF.
Target-specific implementation claim: the immediately preceding request explicitly enumerates the added and revised FAQ content, and the freelancer reports all requested updates are in place.
The new referral-validity and reward messages establish concrete user-facing rules that require corresponding FAQ explanations of accepted, missing, and rejected referrals.
The client unambiguously accepts the proposal that only replacement-contract NFTs participate in the active systems, requiring the FAQ's random-owner explanation to exclude old-contract NFTs.
The client states that a referral-free purchase should create six tickets and a commission allocated by weighted draw, changing the published no-referral reward explanation.

value_updates.approved_faq_copy: Retain the approved FAQ copy, remove the assertion that a referral-free purchase must create six tickets, and state that its $10 commission is allocated by weighted draw among eligible NFT owners.
value_updates.fiat_buyer_rewards_faq_section: Retain the approved fiat-buyer FAQ content, remove the requirement that a missing referral creates six tickets, and state that the $10 no-referral commission is allocated by weighted draw among eligible NFT owners.
value_updates.beginner_rewards_collection_faq_section: Retain the approved beginner rewards content, remove the requirement that a referral-free purchase creates six tickets, and explain that its $10 commission is allocated by weighted draw among eligible NFT owners.
value_updates.no_referral_rewards_faq_section: State that the $10 commission from a referral-free purchase is allocated by weighted draw among eligible NFT owners; do not assert a six-ticket requirement.

verdicts.decision_note: The client retracts the mandatory six-ticket rule but clearly retains weighted allocation of the $10 no-referral commission; the FAQ must omit the unresolved ticket count rather than present it as a rule.
The client establishes the acceptance rule that each non-promotional mint produces one commission and one ticket, including rewards distributed through the weighted draw.

value_updates.approved_faq_copy: Retain the approved FAQ copy, but state that a coded referral produces a $20 commission and that a no-code mint produces an $18 commission assigned randomly; each non-promotional mint still produces one ticket and one commission.
value_updates.fiat_buyer_rewards_faq_section: Retain the approved fiat-buyer FAQ content, but state that coded referrals produce $20 commissions and no-code mints produce $18 commissions assigned randomly.
value_updates.beginner_rewards_collection_faq_section: Retain the approved beginner rewards content, but explain that coded referrals produce $20 commissions and no-code mints produce $18 commissions assigned randomly.
value_updates.no_referral_rewards_faq_section: State that each non-promotional no-code mint produces one ticket and an $18 commission, both assigned randomly and reflected in the reporting interfaces.

verdicts.decision_note: The source distinguishes $20 coded-referral commissions from $18 no-code commissions; the provisional Event omitted the no-code amount and would leave stale FAQ content.
The client accepts the explicit reward logic of four tickets plus $35 for coded referrals and six tickets plus $12 for randomly assigned no-code rewards, requiring consistent FAQ copy.

value_updates.approved_faq_copy: Retain the approved FAQ copy, but change coded-referral reward explanations to use a $12 commission and identify the associated prize draw as $1,250; preserve existing ticket counts, no-code rewards, and unrelated content.
value_updates.fiat_buyer_rewards_faq_section: Retain the approved fiat-buyer FAQ content, but change coded-referral rewards to a $12 commission and a ticket for the $1,250 prize draw; preserve existing ticket counts and no-code rewards.
value_updates.beginner_rewards_collection_faq_section: Retain the approved beginner rewards content, but change coded-referral rewards to a $12 commission and a ticket for the $1,250 prize draw; preserve existing ticket counts and no-code rewards.
value_updates.coded_referral_commission_copy: State that an accepted coded referral gives the chosen NFT holder a $12 commission and a ticket for the $1,250 prize draw.

verdicts.decision_note: The client supplies new user-facing coded-referral reward wording; updating the existing coded_referral_commission_copy prevents the prior $35 value from remaining stale.
The client approves creation and configuration of a Discord community, but the source does not request FAQ publication or establish that Discord is already available as a support channel.
The exchange identifies a manual prize-claim control visible only during the eligibility window, making the FAQ's earlier automatic-payout explanation obsolete.
